newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki ends easier, cautiously eyeing U.S.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki ends easier, cautiously eyeing U.S.

text.p: Shares ended a shade weaker on Monday with a cautious mood creeping in after six consecutive record closes by the Dow industrials in the United States and with volumes sinking to summertime levels, brokers said.

The FOX stock futures index ended 0.23 percent lower at 1,078.22, while the all-share HEX closed off 0.19 percent at 3,137.48 points. Volume was 322 million markka, with telecom group Nokia accounting for over 40 percent of the total.

"It's is the same old story. When the U.S. market rises, people here start selling -- it's not just caution, it's lunacy," one market analyst said, pointing to Helsinki's underperformance versus Wall Street in recent sessions.

But others cited a variety of reasons for the cautious tone, including the European Union's Amsterdam summit on monetary union, and said that they expected another quiet day on Tuesday ahead of U.S. CPI data due at 1230 GMT.
A cautionary message on inflation from the Bank of Finland during the session had little impact on shares, but pushed bond yields up, and brokers said it did not help sentiment.

"It threw a question mark up into the air. The market didn't really need this right now," one broker said, after the central bank said risks of accelerating inflation had increased, though it would not change monetary policy now.

Brokers said interest rate-sensitive financials softened slightly after the central bank's report, with banking group Merita ending off 0.20 markka at 16.30, down from an intraday high of 16.90 markka.
The market was supported by Nokia, which steadily traded in a narrow range and closed up 0.40 markka at 364.90.
Consumer goods and industrial kitchenware maker Hackman rose on a big in-house deal brokered at Carnegie at 185.00 markka per share, and ended up 6.00 markka at 183.00.

Food, feed and chemicals group Raisio fell 16.00 markka to 404.00 in fair seven million markka volume. Brokers said Raisio's conference for equity analysts on Friday had left some expectations unfulfilled.
Some investors had apparently been waiting for faster progress from Raisio on improving the export prospects of its Benecol margarine business, brokers said.
But no collapse was in view for Raisio. "I think the share will stabilise at these levels," one broker said.
Forestries were somewhat softer due to the stronger markka, one broker said. UPM-Kymmene closed fair-volume trade down 0.60 markka at 123.30.
